doc.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995

title: Freddie Green, steady influence and golf
summary: Freddie Green was retiring and steady, and he and Marshall Royal turned Joe from tennis to golf.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Can you tell us a little more about Freddie Green?

Oh, what can I tell you about Freddie? He was just a wonderful steady influence going through the band all the time. He was very retiring, you know he never got in the way or showed off or was obvious anywhere, he just was there, pounding away and being sweet and charming.
Besides being the rock of the rhythm section he was the rock of the people too.

Yes. He was also a very keen golfer. He was responsible for Joe becoming a golf junkie because Joe joined the band with tennis rackets, but he probably has told you. And within a very short time, nobody played tennis, so they hauled him out on the golf course, Freddie Green and Marshall Royal I think. And from then on he was lost to golf and the tennis racket rotted away somewhere.
We just lost Marshall as you know.
